target: workflow.sh merge — a project plugin-region absent from the template is reported as orphaned and its body is kept verbatim, not deleted
cmd: source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/workflow.sh"; source "$FIXTURES/workflow-fixture.sh"; wf_file project.js '// top' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=legacy owner=plugin' 'console.log("legacy code");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=legacy' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'console.log("hi");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '// bottom'; wf_file template.js '// top' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'console.log("hi");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '// bottom'; cp project.js expected.js; VERDICT=$(workflow_merge project.js template.js '//' '{}'); MATCH=$(cmp -s project.js expected.js && echo true || echo false); BODY=$(cat project.js); jq -n --argjson v "$VERDICT" --argjson m "$MATCH" --arg body "$BODY" '{verdict:$v, match:$m, body:$body}'
_note: Upstream dropping a region (e.g. retiring a build-prompt sub-block) must never silently delete the project's copy — it's reported as orphaned so a human can decide, and the merge leaves the file byte-identical (cmp against a pre-merge copy) rather than stripping the now-unrecognized block.
